title.title: A dimension-free log-Sobolev inequality
title.subtitle: Claim: log-concave laws with $a$-subgaussian marginals satisfy log-Sobolev with constant $C a^2$, in every dimension

plain: If a random cloud has thin tails in every direction, is it as tame as a bell curve, in any dimension?

beats.text: How the log-Sobolev constant can grow with dimension $n$: orders only, constants omitted
Bobkov's criterion gives order $n\,a^2$; Bizeul reached about $\sqrt{n}\,a^2$
Claim: a constant $C a^2$, the same in every dimension

steps: Suppose a sequence of such laws makes the constant blow up
Heat flow and Gaussian channel identities describe its fluctuations
The two descriptions disagree: no such sequence exists

achievement.label: Bizeul's conjecture (2023)
achievement.context: Before: constants of order $n\,a^2$ (Bobkov), then about $\sqrt{n}\,a^2$ (Bizeul)
achievement.note: A 2023 conjecture, not a classical one; needs a density and centring

verify.detail: No Lean: a 65-page contradiction argument, not formalized
verify.ourCheck: We read the paper and abstract; nothing here is machine-checked

voice.text: How fast can the constant grow with dimension? Known bounds grew with root n.
Assume a worst case; heat flow describes it in two clashing ways.
Claimed: one constant, the same in every dimension.

sources.quote: Conjectured by P. Bizeul (2023, his Conjecture 2

satisfies Ent_μ(f^2) <= C a^2 ∫|Df|^2 dμ for all smooth compactly supported f, in every dimension
requires a Lebesgue density (full-dimensional) and centering
